headline_marked: Death penalty for [[enforced disappearance criminalized]] by Cabinet
headline: Death penalty for enforced disappearance criminalized by Cabinet
summary: The Bangladesh Cabinet has approved a draft law making enforced disappearance a crime, with the maximum penalty being death.
details: The Bangladesh Cabinet has officially approved a draft law that criminalizes enforced disappearance, marking a significant legal shift in the country's human rights framework.
Under the proposed legislation, the act of enforced disappearance will be treated as a crime, and those found guilty will face severe penalties.
The most striking provision of the draft law is the maximum penalty of the death sentence, which will be applied if the victim of the disappearance dies.
This move comes as part of a broader effort to address long-standing concerns regarding missing persons and state-sponsored disappearances in Bangladesh.
The draft law will now move forward for final legislative approval to be enacted into law.
caption:
Death penalty for enforced disappearance? The Cabinet has approved a draft law to criminalize it.

The Bangladesh Cabinet has officially approved a draft law that criminalizes enforced disappearance, marking a significant legal shift in the country's human rights framework.

Under the proposed legislation, the act of enforced disappearance will be treated as a crime, and those found guilty will face severe penalties.

The most striking provision of the draft law is the maximum penalty of the death sentence, which will be applied if the victim of the disappearance dies.

This move comes as part of a broader effort to address long-standing concerns regarding missing persons and state-sponsored disappearances in Bangladesh.

The draft law will now move forward for final legislative approval to be enacted into law.

#Bangladesh #HumanRights #Law #CabinetDecision #Justice

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News, The Daily Star

headline: Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Walid Al-Khereiji arrives in Dhaka on official visit
summary: The Saudi official is on a two-day government visit to the capital to strengthen bilateral ties.
details: Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Walid Al-Khereiji has arrived in Dhaka for a two-day official government visit.
The visit is aimed at discussing bilateral relations and enhancing cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Bangladesh.
During his stay, the Deputy Foreign Minister is expected to hold meetings with high-ranking government officials to discuss various strategic interests.
